Town in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. | Location of Beckum within Warendorf district |. | Beckum  is located in Germany Beckum  Beckum Show map of Germany  Beckum  is located in North Rhine-Westphalia Beckum  Beckum Show map of North Rhine-Westphalia |. pagename=Beckum,\_Germany¶ms=51\_45\_18\_N\_8\_02\_25\_E\_type:city(37133)\_region:DE-NW 51°45′18″N 8°02′25″E﻿ / ﻿51.75500°N 8.04028°E﻿ / 51.75500; 8.04028]"}}" id="mwJw" about="#mwt12" typeof="mw:Extension/indicator"> |. **Beckum** (German pronunciation:  ⓘ; Westphalian: *Biäkem*) is a town in the northern part of North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. The town quickly expanded to an area of over 22 km2 (8.5 sq miles). In 1816 Beckum became the district town of Beckum district. As of 1 January 1975, the Beckum and Warendorf districts merged into one, and Warendorf remained district town of the whole area. Ahlen, Beckum's neighbour 11 km (7 miles) to the west, is the largest town in Warendorf District.

He is a member of the Christian Democratic Union "Christian Democratic Union (Germany)") (CDU), part of the European People's Party. On 1 July 2010 McAllister was elected Minister-President of the state of Lower Saxony, succeeding Christian Wulff, who resigned following his election as President of Germany. In the 2014 European elections, McAllister was elected a Member of the European Parliament as the CDU's top candidate in Lower Saxony. A lawyer by profession, he served as chairman of the CDU parliamentary group in the Lower Saxon Parliament from 2003 to 2010 and was elected chairman of the state party in 2008.
